Q0104

“Virtue does not come from money, but from virtue come money and…” — Socrates (Plato, Apology 30a–b)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Plato, Apology 30a–b. Theme: virtue.

Quotes / Socrates / Q0104

English

Virtue does not come from money, but from virtue come money and all other good things for human beings.
Thinker Socrates
School Socratic School
Source Plato, Apology 30a–b
Theme Virtue
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Plato, Apology 30a–b and files it under Socratic School. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Socrates

Socrates (c. 470/469–399 BCE) was an Athenian citizen who wrote nothing and yet redirected Greek philosophy from cosmology toward ethics and the care of the soul.

How to read this passage

Virtue ethics asks not only which acts are right, but what kind of person one becomes. Courage, justice, temperance, and wisdom are classic Western lists; Confucian ren and yi offer related but distinct vocabularies. This passage enters that discussion through virtue.

Concepts in this quote

Virtue
Virtue names excellences of character—habits of perception and action oriented toward the good.
